params.question: Which combination of clinical findings allows classification of the type of abortion at initial presentation, even before ultrasound is available?

answers.text: Serum β-hCG level, progesterone level, endometrial thickness, and fetal crown-rump length

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: These are laboratory and ultrasonographic parameters, not bedside clinical findings. Classification of abortion type is made on physical examination before these results are available.

answers.text: Maternal age, parity, gestational age, and previous obstetric history

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: These are historical features important for risk assessment but do not determine the type of abortion at the current presentation — classification depends on the current clinical state.

answers.text: Status of the cervical os, uterine size for dates, passage of tissue, and presence of infection

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. These four clinical anchors — cervical os status (open vs closed), uterine size relative to dates, whether products of conception have been passed, and whether infection is present — allow classification of abortion type on physical examination alone.

answers.text: Haemoglobin level, blood group, coagulation profile, and platelet count

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: These are supportive laboratory investigations for assessing the severity of blood loss, not for classifying the type of abortion.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the four clinical anchors used to classify abortion: cervical os status (open vs closed), uterine size for dates, whether tissue has been passed, and presence of infection.
Well done! The four clinical anchors — os status, uterine size, tissue passage, and infection — are the bedside findings that classify abortion type before any investigation.

interactions.label: The American Society for Reproductive Medicine (ASRM) defines recurrent pregnanc

params.question: The American Society for Reproductive Medicine (ASRM) defines recurrent pregnancy loss as three or more consecutive pregnancy losses before 20 weeks of gestation.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: The ASRM actually defines recurrent pregnancy loss as two or more ultrasound-confirmed losses — a less stringent threshold than the RCOG/ESHRE definition of three or more consecutive losses before 20 weeks. For NMC examinations, always state which definition you are using.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — the ASRM uses a lower threshold of two or more clinical (ultrasound-confirmed) losses, recognising the emotional burden and likelihood of identifying a treatable cause. The three-or-more consecutive losses definition belongs to the RCOG and ESHRE.

interactions.label: Which clinical finding, when present, is pathognomonic of a hydatidiform mole?

params.question: Which clinical finding, when present, is pathognomonic of a hydatidiform mole?

answers.text: Uterus measuring larger than expected for gestational age

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A uterus large-for-dates is characteristic of a complete mole but can also occur in multiple gestation, polyhydramnios, and uterine fibroids — it is not pathognomonic.

Correct. Passage of grape-like (hydatid) vesicles is pathognomonic of a hydatidiform mole — these are swollen chorionic villi that are diagnostic when seen by the naked eye or on histological examination.

answers.text: Heavy vaginal bleeding in the first trimester

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Heavy vaginal bleeding in the first trimester occurs in many conditions — threatened abortion, ectopic pregnancy, and cervical pathology — and is not specific to molar pregnancy.

answers.text: Serum β-hCG level markedly higher than expected for gestational age

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Markedly elevated β-hCG supports the diagnosis of a molar pregnancy but is not pathognomonic — levels can be elevated in normal multiple pregnancies and some germ cell tumours.

overallFeedback.feedback: The pathognomonic finding is passage of grape-like vesicles — other features like bleeding, large-for-dates uterus, and elevated β-hCG are suggestive but not specific to molar pregnancy.
Correct! Grape-like vesicles (hydatid vesicles) are pathognomonic of a hydatidiform mole — always inspect passed tissue carefully.

interactions.label: After suction evacuation for incomplete abortion, which of the following provide

params.question: After suction evacuation for incomplete abortion, which of the following provides the structural proof that products of conception have been successfully removed?

answers.text: Feeling a gritty sensation as the curette contacts the uterine wall

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The intraoperative gritty feel is a useful tactile sign that the cavity is empty, but it is subjective and does not confirm the nature of the tissue removed — it is not structural proof.

answers.text: Identifying chorionic villi on visual inspection of the aspirated tissue

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Identifying chorionic villi in the aspirated tissue provides the structural proof that pregnancy tissue has been removed — this can be done immediately by examining the tissue in a bowl of saline in the procedure room.

answers.text: Performing a post-procedure transvaginal ultrasound showing an empty cavity

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Post-procedure ultrasound is a valuable adjunct and the third step in the confirmation sequence, but it may not always be available — visual identification of chorionic villi provides more immediate and definitive tissue confirmation.

answers.text: Observing that vaginal bleeding has stopped within 30 minutes of the procedure

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Cessation of bleeding is reassuring but unreliable as confirmation — retained products can present with delayed haemorrhage or endometritis hours to days later.

overallFeedback.feedback: The three-step confirmation sequence is: (1) intraoperative feel of the uterine wall, (2) visual inspection of aspirate for chorionic villi — this is the structural proof, and (3) post-procedure ultrasound where available.
Exactly right — visual identification of chorionic villi in the aspirate provides immediate structural proof of successful evacuation, even without ultrasound.
